newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony suspends Japan chip plant output after quake.
newsitem.headline: Sony suspends Japan chip plant output after quake.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Thursday it had temporarily suspended operations at a semiconductor plant after an earthquake shook the southern Japan island of Kyushu on Wednesday.
A Sony spokesman said operations at the company's Kokubu plant in Kyushu's Kagoshima Prefecture were suspended to check for damage to its facilities from the tremor.
The plant's output includes integrated circuit chips and liquid crystal displays (LCDs), the spokesman said. He declined to give the size of production at the plant.
An official at the Kokubu plant said: "There are some parts of the production line that need to be fixed,"
He said the line was expected to resume operations by Friday.
Several other Japanese high-tech companies which have plants in the region said they stopped production lines after the earthquake but had since resumed operations.
NEC Corp said it stopped operations at its Kagoshima plant, which makes thin film transistor LCDs, late on Wednesday, but had since resumed production as there was no damage from the earthquake.
The moderately strong earthquake measuring 6.2 on the Richter scale caused minor injuries to at least six people.
Japan's Meteorological Agency said the earthquake hit the island at 5.31 p.m. (0831 GMT) on Wednesday with its epicentre near the city of Kagoshima, 800 km (500 miles) southwest of Tokyo.
A number of fairly strong tremors continued to shake the region after the initial quake, and agency officials warned that aftershocks could continue in the area for a while.
